messages:
dinesh: Hey team — trying to run the starter hello-world sample after renaming my workspace, and the curl call returns 403. Not sure what changed.

Here is the exact command I ran:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RI_KEY\" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hello"}'
```

Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` with body `{"error":"billing_required","message":"Organization requires a valid payment method"}`

anne: Thanks for the report — can you confirm whether the workspace rename also changed org membership or billing assignment? Quick question: is $RI_KEY a user key tied to the org or a workspace/service key?

dinesh: It's a personal API key I created earlier under the same org. I renamed the workspace name only (display name) via the web UI. I didn't touch org-level settings. The key was working yesterday.

jordan: We rolled out a billing gate change yesterday that started enforcing valid payment methods for some trial->paid org transitions. Could be related. dinesh, can you paste the exact org id (redacted ok) and whether the org shows a card in Settings > Billing?

dinesh: Org shows a card but the UI shows "expires Oct 2024" — that might be the cause. I didn't realize it had an expired card.

billing-bot: Automated notice: Payment method on file for org `rwd-2390` attempted renewal and failed. Please update billing details at https://console.redwood.run/orgs/rwd-2390/billing :card_with_warning:

anne: If the org payment method failed, API returns billing_required for any usage that would consume beyond free credits. Two options: 1) update the card, or 2) switch your request to a workspace with active credits / use a service account tied to a different billable org.

dinesh: Is there a CLI way to confirm which org my token maps to? Don't want to re-add card if I've accidentally created a new personal org.

cli-bot: You can run:
```bash
ri whoami --json
# or
ri orgs list --token $RI_KEY
```
That will show the org id and billing status columns (if you have permission). Also `ri env export` prints WORKSPACE_ID if you used the starter.

jordan: Another temporary workaround: create a new service API key under a different org that has an active card, or use a service account from infra. We'll help if you need one.

dinesh: Ran `ri whoami` — output shows org id rwd-2390 and role owner. Confirmed billing status: FAILED_RENEWAL. Re-added a new card in the console.

anne: Great. After you update the card, tokens should be allowed again. If you still get 403 after adding a valid card, try regenerating the API key and re-running the sample (sometimes cached edge policy takes a minute).

dinesh: Updated card and regenerated key. Re-ran the same curl and now getting 200. Streaming response starts OK. First successful sample run after the rename! :tada:

Response snippet:
```json
{"id":"gen_01F...","status":"succeeded","output":"Hello!"}
```

anne: Awesome — thanks for confirming. I'll add a short note to onboarding docs: renaming workspaces doesn't usually affect billing, but expired cards will now block usage more aggressively (policy change).

jordan: Filing a small telemetry ticket to make the "expired card" state show a console banner for workspace owners (so individuals see it sooner).

dinesh: Thanks all — unblocked and back to experimenting. If anyone wants me to test the new banner, happy to help.

anne: Appreciate it. Closing the loop here; filing a docs PR and a follow-up task. :white_check_mark:
